messages:
dana-support: Hey team — customer acme-inc reported a sudden spike of KMS Decrypt failures from their EC2 fleet after the key rotation we did yesterday. They assume-role into account `prod-app-role` then call KMS decrypt and get AccessDenied / MissingEncryptionContext. CloudTrail Decrypt events for those calls also do NOT include an encryptionContext field. Can someone triage?

sre_oncall: I can take initial triage. Is this affecting production requests or only a smaller repro?

dana-support: Impacting prod traffic for one tenant (bursting errors, customer-facing latency+errors). Repro steps below, customer supplied logs.

leo: Paste the error text and a snippet of the CloudTrail event please. Also which alias/key-id?

dana-support: Error output from SDK: 
```
Aws::KMS::Errors::AccessDenied: Access denied for decrypt
message: "User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh because encryptionContext mismatch"
```
CloudTrail decrypt event (redacted): 
```
{ eventName: "Decrypt", awsRegion: "us-west-2", userIdentity: { arn: "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/prod-app-role/session123" }, requestParameters: { ciphertextBlob: "<binary>" } }
```
Note: no `encryptionContext` in requestParameters. Key alias: alias/acme-prod-data.

marta: Two quick possibilities that come up frequently: 1) the caller isn't supplying the encryption context (app change or client side bug), or 2) something in the mid-tier (proxy, sidecar) used to add the context stopped injecting it after the rotation or configuration change.

sam: Also check key policy and any Grants — if the key requires a specific encryptionContext (via Condition in key policy) and the request doesn't include it, KMS will deny. But CloudTrail missing the encryptionContext indicates the request never sent it.

dana-support: Repro steps customer provided: 
1) EC2 assume-role: `aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/prod-app-role --role-session-name ci`
2) export STS creds
3) `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh`
-> fails with AccessDenied as above.

leo: Try a manual decrypt with an explicit encryption-context param from the EC2 instance to confirm. `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob --key-id ... --encryption-context Application=acme` If that succeeds, it proves the key+role are OK but the app/agent isn't sending the context.

dana-support: Ran that manually from an affected instance — when we include `--encryption-context Application=acme` it succeeds. When omitted it fails. So the key is enforcing a context and the instance doesn't send it by default.

kms-bot: NOTE: Key alias/arn alias/acme-prod-data rotated at 2025-03-10T18:23:11Z by ops@redwood. Rotation: AUTOMATIC.

marta: Given that, two parallel actions: 1) short-term mitigation — create a grant allowing prod-app-role to decrypt without encryptionContext so customer recovers, 2) long-term — find why the proxy/agent stopped inserting encryptionContext or why client library change removed it. I'll check ingress proxy and sidecar config.

sam: Ok to create a short-lived grant for that role, but limit scope and expiry. Use `aws kms create-grant` with Principals set to the role ARN and Operations=[Decrypt] and set Constraints? KMS grants don't let you ignore encryptionContext constraints in the key policy; if the key policy enforces encryptionContext via Condition, granting won't bypass it. We should instead temporarily relax the key policy (add an explicit Allow for the role for kms:Decrypt without the Condition) or add a separate key policy statement scoped to the role. Both require security review.

leo: Quick check: can we confirm the key policy has a Condition for `kms:EncryptionContext:Application`? Dana, can you paste the key policy snippet?

dana-support: Key policy statement (redacted): 
```
"Condition": { "StringEquals": { "kms:EncryptionContext:Application": "acme" } }
```
So yes, policy requires that.

sam: Given that, the minimal path to restore is: temporarily add a policy statement allowing `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/prod-app-role` kms:Decrypt without the encryptionContext Condition, with an expiry by tag/managed process, and log it in the incident. We'll coordinate with infra to ensure rollback once client fix is deployed.

marta: I will look at the proxy logs now — checking for recent deploys that could strip headers. If the proxy is injecting `x-kms-encctx` header that the client maps to encryptionContext, a deploy could have changed header forwarding.

dana-support: Confirmed: the sidecar was recently bumped from 1.12.2 -> 1.13.0 two nights ago for security patch. Release notes show a change to header sanitization. This likely stripped the `X-Encryption-Context` header.

leo: That matches. Plan: 1) add temporary key policy allowance for role, 2) notify customer and enable fix (sidecar rollback or update mapping), 3) after customer sends correct encryptionContext again, remove allowance and verify CloudTrail shows encryptionContext.

sam: I'll prepare the policy change snippet and the exact AWS CLI to apply. Example policy statement to add (apply to the key resource via kms:PutKeyPolicy or admin): 
```
{
  "Sid": "TemporaryAllowProdAppRoleDecrypt",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/prod-app-role" },
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
Note: we should scope Resource/Condition more narrowly in the real change and add an explicit expiry checklist in the incident ticket.

dana-support: Applying the temporary key policy change now in us-west-2 (with sam on the call). Will tag change `incident/1749456123` and add expiry note for 72h.

kms-bot: Policy change detected for key/abcd-efgh by dana-support at 2025-03-11T02:20:07Z.

dana-support: After policy change, customer confirms decrypts from EC2 succeed without providing encryptionContext. They pushed a sidecar rollback the same morning which also restored the header injection.

marta: Action items: 1) eng-platform to roll forward sidecar fix that preserves header forwarding (marta) — PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/sidecar/pull/421, 2) customer to update app to explicitly set encryptionContext (dana-support to coordinate), 3) eng-security to remove temporary policy allowance after validation (sam).

sam: I'll schedule removal in 48-72h after we see 24h of clean decrypts with encryptionContext present in CloudTrail. Also will add a playbook entry for similar rotation incidents.

sre_oncall: Closing loop: severity reduced, customer recovered, temporary policy applied then to be revoked after verification. I'll create an incident summary doc and move to postmortem if needed. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

dana-support: Thanks team — I'll follow up with the customer and file the incident ticket with logs and timeline.
